data.why: The app generates its own synthetic candidate/reference NetCDF pair in memory via the 'Load demonstration data' button (cdfuse/sample.py), so no files need to be copied or written.

goals: Load the built-in demonstration candidate/reference dataset pair and run a full comparison end to end
Confirm or correct the auto-detected time/latitude/longitude coordinates for each dataset
Choose temporal aggregation, aggregation statistic, and spatial alignment method appropriate for the data
Select evaluation metrics (NSE, KGE, PBIAS, RMSE, MAE, Bias, Correlation) and interpret the per-cell score maps
Inspect the summary statistics table and coverage to judge how well the candidate reproduces the reference
Download per-metric outputs (PNG map, NetCDF, GeoTIFF, CSV) and the full ZIP archive with run report

review.summary: The tree matches CDFuse's stated purpose and stages well: align a candidate dataset to a reference in time and space, score each cell, map the scores, and export them. The ten screens I checked all support their nodes. It needs fixes before filing: the main step of uploading your own pair (with choosing the variable) and the boundary option are missing, and one export claim (correlation.csv) is contradicted by the replay.
